title: The Concept of Categorical Imperative
text:
Immanuel Kant's Categorical Imperative presents a fundamental principle of moral action that is necessary regardless of inclination or desired outcome. It stipulates that moral laws must be universalizable, meaning one should act only according to that maxim which can be willed as a universal law without contradiction.

Furthermore, the formulation demands treating humanity always as an end and never merely as a means. This emphasizes the intrinsic worth and dignity of every rational being, arguing against any action where individuals are used solely for external goals or profit.
